note: A single site on a bare dirt clearing at the end of a spur road and a secondary two-track driveway off Rock Run Road. The agency says the site is not recommended for low-clearance vehicles, and cautions that the dirt or gravel forest roads may not suit low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. Stone fire ring; no table, toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: 019 Packman still listed, Drive-In, RV/Tent/Trailer categories, max vehicle and equipment length 30 ft, back-in dirt driveway 30 ft, grades Slight; count 1 and 30 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Year-round confirmed; sells in all five windows. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri and PASDA leaf-off): pin on the east edge of a bare dirt clearing roughly 35 x 40 m, open to the sky, at the end of a track coming up from the south-south-west; pin on site. NHD: nothing within 200 m; not waterfront.
flags: CRITERIA flag (single-site entry; kept with the wording in the note, the owner decides): the page says 'This campsite is accessed by a spur road and then a secondary two-track driveway off Rock Run Rd. Not recommended for low-clearance vehicles.' That is a site-specific agency statement about the access, stronger than the district caution. It is not a 4WD statement and no grade is Severe, so ruling 11's automatic grounds do not apply; if a motorhome counts as low-clearance here the entry has no site left. The stored note already said 'Rough access: high clearance advised.'

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Caution: This campsite is accessed by state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large RVs.' 'Site Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Surface: Dirt', 'Site Height/Overhead Clearance: 20'. No Severe grade, no 4WD or wet-weather statement, no closure. The page also carries the district-wide 'Road and Travel Alert' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' boilerplate (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).

Figures: 'Max Vehicle Length: 30' and 'Equipment Length: 30' beside 'Length of shortest side of spur to the wheelstop: 20' on a 30 x 25 ft site with a 30-ft driveway. Max Vehicle and Equipment Length are over 23 ft but the spur figure is under it: kept at 30 ft with all figures in the sites note.

ATV check (ruling 1): the DCNR Susquehannock ATV Trail brochure names a 'Rock Run Trailhead ... along Rock Run Road' with 'a small parking lot for trucks and vehicles with trailers. Camping is permitted at this trailhead.' That is NOT this site: the DCNR GIS layer carries the trailhead camp as a separate record, '029 Rock Run ATV' (41.75021,-77.75290, siteId 29123), about 1.6 km south-west of 019 Packman (41.76121,-77.74019). The Packman page says nothing about ATVs or parking. Kept.
NAME: the stored name carries the site's own name and road as the booking system gives them ('Site, Loop: 019 Packman, Rock Run Rd'); nothing to change.
Equestrian check: the Susquehannock camping page names the Dyer and Horsey Hilton equestrian areas; this entry is neither and its page(s) list no horse category.

Susquehannock advisories page (read 2026-11-10): district office closure Oct 17-18, 2026; Rausch Road reopened July 31, 2025; 'Stay Alert for ATVs on Roads' (the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail uses some PennDOT, township and forest roads); a dust advisory. No road closure, gate, bridge limit or timber-sale notice, and nothing on this entry's road. The camping page publishes no seasonal closure or site rotation.
